questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to keep chickens at home
What chickens can teach us about hierarchies at work
Why managers have too many meetings
How farmers can get more eggs from each of their chickens
questions.why: They discuss hierarchies and an experiment with chickens that Margaret Heffernan links to the workplace.

questions.q: What joke does Catherine make about managers?
options: They are paid too much
They never come to work
They are always late
Their meetings stop the workers from working
questions.why: She says the managers 'have meetings that stop the workers doing the work!'

questions.q: In the experiment, what two groups of chickens were compared?
options: Young chickens and old chickens
Wild chickens and farm chickens
Average chickens and super-chickens that laid more eggs
Male chickens and female chickens
questions.why: Researchers compared average chickens with super-chickens, which have above average egg production.

questions.q: What happened to the average flock over six generations?
options: It kept getting better and laid more eggs
Most of the chickens died before the end of the experiment
It stayed exactly the same
It stopped laying eggs
questions.why: Margaret Heffernan says the average flock 'just gets better and better' and egg production increases.

options: It laid the most eggs of any flock in the experiment
Only three were left, because they killed the rest
The chickens became average
It was moved to another farm
questions.why: She says all but three are dead, 'because the other three have killed the rest'.

questions.q: Why does Margaret Heffernan say 'And that's what we do at work'?
options: To show people at work also succeed by holding others back
To suggest that office workers should start keeping their own chickens
To say that offices need more workers
To explain why eggs are cheap
questions.why: The super-chickens succeeded by suppressing others' productivity, and she compares this to work.

questions.q: According to Catherine, when can hierarchies at work go wrong?
options: When workers are paid too little
When everyone is equal
When there are too few managers to organise all the workers
When managers get in the way of workers
questions.why: She says some managers show their productivity by interfering with the productivity of the workers.

questions.q: What kind of hierarchy works well for chickens?
options: One forced on them by farmers
One with a single leader and no levels
One they create among themselves
One that changes every day
questions.why: Heffernan says it's one 'they create among themselves, rather than one that's imposed upon them'.
